title: run.record.v1: the run record as the registry stores it
description: STORAGE record. This is the JSON document the daemon's registry keeps for one run (core/recursion_core/control/registry.py). The twelve required fields are exactly what is stored today and none of them changes in version 1, including 'start_key' and 'stop_attestation' in today's shapes. The other fields are optional additions: each is either absent or carries a value, and null is not used for them. NONE of the additions is ever copied from a request's params: principal comes from the way the request came in, owner from that principal, budget from the quota part of start normalisation, route, route_decision and workspace from the validated output of start normalisation, and session_id and turn_id only from the daemon's own session service. RESERVED, and refused by this schema until the lane that owns Stop defines them: a 'launch_manifest' field, and a stored attestation whose proof is 'removed'. What a client reads from run.status and run.list is a different record, run.view.v1.

engine_as_given.description: The engine name the start asked for, as given: run.start accepts any non-empty string and a start that names an engine with no route is recorded as start_failed with that name.

stored_state.description: starting: the launch intent is written and no cgroup is recorded yet. start_failed: the launch path refused or failed. running: the unit's cgroup is recorded. stop_pending: a Stop was asked and is not confirmed. stopped: terminal, and stored only with an attestation.

cgroup.description: The unit's cgroup path, or null until the launch is recorded.

cgroup_marker.description: An identity for that cgroup which a new path never inherits, or null while there is no cgroup.

generation.description: Rises by one with every stored write. A write names the generation it read; one that names an older generation is refused.

stop.description: null until a Stop is asked. requested is true only once the cleanup request was sent to the cgroup named by this object's own cgroup and cgroup_marker, which are written at that moment (control/api.py, _stop_attempt) and are absent on a Stop kept as an intent.

start_key.description: null for a start with no client_key. Otherwise what a retried start is compared with. The three required fields are today's: the key, the engine, and the SHA-256 of the prompt's UTF-8 bytes (the prompt itself is not stored). intent_version and intent_sha256 are new in version 1, optional, and always come together: they are the only place the identity of a request is kept. The daemon computes the INTENT from what the client sent, never from a digest the client supplies. Version 1 is the JSON, with sorted keys, UTF-8 and no insignificant space, of {engine as given or null, prompt_sha256, workspace as given or null, hand_pick or null, containment_level or null, session_id or null}, where missing and null are the same; intent_sha256 is its SHA-256. A retry is looked up by (tenant, client_key) before anything is normalised: with a stored intent, an equal intent_sha256 is a retry and anything else is refused client_key_reused; with a key that has no intent (a legacy key), a request whose intent has only engine and prompt is compared as today, and a request with any other field set is refused client_key_reused.

stop_attestation.description: null unless the run is stopped. The stored proof is today's and only today's: 'empty', which says that the cgroup named here was read empty and every member listed was gone, at this generation of the record. A stored proof of 'removed' is RESERVED: the lane that owns Stop adds it together with the registry's own proof checks, and until then this schema refuses it. A reader that meets a proof it does not know treats the run as NOT stopped.

launch_route.description: The route the launch really used: the effective launch snapshot, shaped like one entry of the operator's routes file (the route part of a 'recursion.route/v0' request, core/recursion_core/routes/contract.py). A retry reuses this snapshot; nothing is routed again. engine, model and connection are always there. The other fields are the route contract's own and are present only when the entry had them. credential_env is the NAME of an environment variable, never a value. 'profile' is the engine adapter's own object.

engine_session_id.description: The engine's own id for its conversation, used to resume or fork it. It is the engine's value and is treated as untrusted text.

continues.description: The run this run continues: the run a fallback took over from after a limit, or the earlier run of a worker that was brought back.

stopped_rules.description: The registry's own rules for 'stopped', which the public view shares.
